findings.title: Duplicate scopes not de-duplicated on init
findings.body: In AdminPermissionsSchema.init the code collects ScopeRepresentation objects into a Set to get rid of duplicities when USERS and CLIENTS share scopes (manage, view, map-roles). ScopeRepresentation does not implement equals/hashCode by name, so the Set contains one object per occurrence (11 objects for 8 distinct names). The realm init then tries to create duplicate scopes named manage/view/map-roles, which can fail or create duplicates for every new realm with admin permissions enabled.

findings.title: Per-client check ignores all-clients grant when specific resource exists
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String) looks up the per-client resource by client id and only if it is null falls back to evaluating the all-clients resource named Clients. If a per-client resource exists (created for any prior per-client permission) the method evaluates only that resource and never evaluates the all-clients resource. An admin granted manage/view/configure/map-roles on all clients is therefore incorrectly denied on any client that happens to have a per-client resource, breaking the documented all-clients fallback.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns type resource as client id
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission iterates resourceStore.findByType for type Clients and adds every granted resource.getName() to the result. The all-type resource itself has type Clients and name Clients, so it is also visited. If the all-clients permission is granted, the returned set contains the bogus id Clients instead of real client ids, and per-client checks do not consider the all-type grant. Callers filtering clients by this set get wrong results.

findings.title: Missing null check before findByResource causes NPE
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel,String) when no per-client resource is found the code loads the all-clients resource via getResourceTypeResource, which can return null if the Clients type resource is missing, and then immediately calls findByResource(server, resource) with that value. Passing null throws NullPointerException/IllegalArgumentException instead of returning false, turning a permission check into a 500 error.

findings.title: getResourceName has no handling for Clients type
findings.body: getResourceName special-cases the Users type to return All users or the username for a user resource, but has no branch for the new Clients type. For client permissions it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is not set for auto-created client resources (name is the client UUID). Permission listings for clients will show null/blank instead of the clientId.

findings.title: Removal listener disabled for V2 leaves orphan authz resources
findings.body: registerListener now only runs when feature ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled. When only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent are ignored and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException so there is no alternative path. Deleting a client in V2 therefore leaves its per-client authorization resource and associated policies orphaned in the store.

findings.title: Wrong Javadoc for requireView methods
findings.body: The interface documents void requireView() as Returns true if canView() returns true and void requireViewClientScopes() as Returns true if canViewClientScopes() returns true. Both methods return void and throw ForbiddenException on denial. The copy-pasted return documentation misleads implementers and callers about the contract.
